 | D43 | Platform positioning + editor/IDE tooling | **Gramaire is positioned as a converter-hub-first, standard-track EBNF format (earn "the standard" via a second real round-trip, not by declaring it) and as a learning/debugging/analysis platform. "One portable Scala drives CLI/Web/JVM/WASM; TypeScript is web-glue only" is codified as a standing architectural rule, not a new direction — the Lab already calls Scala.js-compiled `core`/`lab` from `worker.ts` rather than reimplementing engine logic in TS. Roadmap additions, in dependency order: (1) **done** — D38 (Bison/yacc import+export) bundled with D39 (comment round-trip) as one unit, tested as `import(export(x))` fidelity, not just "parses"; (2) Tier-1 LSP server (JVM, native-image, reuses the existing `cli` packaging) gated on Phase F's incremental core (D18/D22) — this is the hinge every client below depends on; (3) VSCode extension as a thin TS activation shell speaking LSP-over-stdio to the same native-image binary, no engine logic in TS; (4) JetBrains plugin embedding the JVM core jar directly (no protocol layer needed — cheaper architecturally, but scored down on effort for platform/maintenance unknowns since the team has no prior JetBrains-plugin experience), sequenced *after* VSCode so the LSP contract is proven first; (5) standalone app as a packaging exercise over the same native-image binary + the Lab's static frontend, last since it is the cheapest once the LSP server exists; (6) MCP server deferred, not rejected — the CLI's JSON output (`emit --backend ir`) already covers stateless agent use, so MCP only earns its keep once Phase F's incremental server holds parse state worth keeping warm across calls.** | Debated internally (2026-07-04): the "standard" framing was contested until tied to a testable round-trip-fidelity bar rather than a positioning claim; LSP-before-editor-clients was contested until framed as risk sequencing (prove the server contract once via the cheapest client before a second, harder-to-iterate-on client depends on it); JetBrains-is-cheap was contested (classloader/plugin-API-skew/no prior experience are real, uncounted costs) and the roadmap value/effort scores below reflect that pushback; MCP was contested on "name the concrete benefit or cut it" grounds and tied explicitly to D22's incremental-as-capability gate rather than treated as a free add-on. New precondition surfaced by the debate: the D29 document-structure contract must be frozen before any editor extension ships syntax/folding logic against it, since a shipped extension hard-codes that contract in a way an IR version bump does not. |
 | D44 | Product rebrand: Gramaire → Gramaire | **Full project rebrand from "Gramaire" to "Gramaire", planned now, executed before GA (a hard pre-GA gate, not a post-launch cleanup) — see `docs/rebrand-gramaire-plan.md` for the scope inventory (~1,714 occurrences across 184 files, the `gramaire.*` Scala package namespace, the native-image CLI binary, the GitHub repo and its non-auto-redirecting Pages URL) and phased sequencing (brand redesign first, then the mechanical package/site/docs rename, then external surfaces). The `.gram`/`.gram.md` file extension is very likely renaming too (`.gram`/`.gram.md`) — the mirror script already implements it — pending final sign-off. The new standalone live-editing notebook page shipped ahead of the full rebrand under the name **"Gramaire Notebook"**; that name is now itself stale (see below) and will need renaming as part of the rebrand's execution, not "no further change" as originally assumed.** | An internal debate (2026-07-04) on scoping "Gramaire" to just the notebook feature versus the whole project concluded the team would have scoped it to the notebook alone — the shipped "Gramaire" wordmark/logomark is a load-bearing pun specifically on "gra-**m**-ark" (the grammar+markdown portmanteau) that doesn't transfer to a new name, so a full rebrand means a genuine brand redesign, not a rename, on top of a ~184-file mechanical migration and a GitHub Pages URL that won't auto-redirect. The product decision overrides that recommendation in favor of the fuller, more distinctive story (grammar and gramaire both descend from the Old French root *gramaire* — "a book you write living things into" fits a live notebook well), gated on GA so the migration has a real deadline rather than drifting. The working target name was "Gramaire" until a 2026-07-05 collision-risk audit found it comprehensively unavailable (GitHub/npm/PyPI/domains) and actively used by a live commercial competitor — the target name changed to **"Gramaire"**, the etymology's own root word, which came back clean on every channel checked. Full trail in `docs/rebrand-gramaire-plan.md`. |
 | D45 | Predicate evaluation during prediction | **Deferred, unscheduled — scoped, not built. See `docs/all-star-port-plan.md`'s Phase 7 for the full breakdown: (1) no `PredicateTransition` exists in the ATN, and the ATN is built from the desugared `Grammar`, not the IR, so `IRRule.predicate` and prediction are disconnected; (2) no JVM-side execution engine exists for ANY action, predicate or value — the Lab only runs actions by `import()`-ing generated JS into the browser's own V8, which has no JVM equivalent; (3) prediction sees raw token lookahead only, never the CST/captured fields a predicate's body might reference, which are only populated after an alt is chosen; (4) executing arbitrary `%lang`-specific code is inherently I/O-shaped, which the cross-compiled, I/O-free `core` cannot host directly. `{%? %}` stays real, parseable, buildable, round-trippable notation — D-predicates/D42's "the predictor evaluates predicates" language was aspirational, not yet implemented.** | Surfaced 2026-07-05 while adding `examples/predicate-guard.gram.md` (a real `{%? %}` + `{% %}` combined example) and fixing an unrelated display bug (`BackendJs.unwrapBinder` leaking a predicate's synthesized binder into the Lab's railroad caption/Lowered Core). Scoping first, rather than building speculatively, matches this plan's own existing "document the gap, revisit as a dedicated effort" pattern (cf. D21 reserving GLR's runtime hook well before D15's engine phase landed) — four independent sub-problems (ATN wiring, a net-new JVM execution engine, a net-new prediction-time data model, and a cross-platform execution boundary respecting the I/O-free gate) is a multi-module architecture project, not a follow-on patch to an example or a bug fix. |
+| D46 | Literal/token/nonterminal/EOF symbol classification | **`LabProtocol.scala`'s `ProductionInfo.rhs` and `RuleFirstFollow.first`/`.follow` changed from `Vector[String]` (pre-rendered, backtick-quoted display text) to `Vector[RenderedSymbol]` (`{text, kind}`, `kind` one of `literal \| token \| nonterminal \| eof`), so the Lab's clients can style each symbol kind distinctly instead of inferring "is this a terminal" from surrounding backticks. Classification is a NAME-KEYED SIDE MAP (`LabApi.classifyTerminals: Map[String, SymbolKind]`), built once from the pre-`GSym` `Sym` tree and deliberately never added as a field on `GSym.Term` itself — `GSym`'s `equals`/`hashCode`/ordering are load-bearing for `Table.scala`'s LR table construction (states are merged/deduped by symbol equality), and that module is explicitly documented as "ported closely, not creatively," so a `kind` field riding along on `GSym.Term` risked silently changing state-merging behavior in a rare symbol-name-collision case. `LrActionInfo` (the Parse trace/Walk tab) deliberately keeps the old string-only `renderSym` — no client need for kind classification there yet.** | Surfaced 2026-07-05/06 from a user question ("how to distinguish between token, rule and string literal?") while chip-printing FIRST/FOLLOW instead of one plain-text set (a companion UI change, not itself an ADR-worthy decision). The user explicitly chose the larger scope over a narrower client-side heuristic: extend the figure grouping (railroad + FIRST/FOLLOW as one semantic unit) to Paper and PDF too, not just the Notebook, and implement the full structured kind distinction now (Scala core + protocol + client) rather than deferring it. `spec/lab-protocol-schema.json`/`site/src/lab/protocol.ts` regenerated to match; the JVM↔JS conformance gate (`check:lab-parity`) confirms parity under the new shape. Rejected: inferring kind client-side from text shape (fragile — a literal and a token can both be bare identifiers depending on the grammar) and adding `kind` to `GSym.Term` directly (the state-merging risk above). |

+- **FIRST/FOLLOW as per-rule chips, not a plain-text set.** A rule's own
+  FIRST/FOLLOW used to render as one space-joined string
+  (``{ `(` `NUMBER` }``) — hard to scan once a FOLLOW set grows past a
+  couple of tokens, and visually inconsistent with the Generated-tables
+  table's own per-token markdown `code` spans a few scrolls down. Each
+  member of `RuleFirstFollow.first`/`.follow` now renders as its own chip
+  (`.gramaire__output-ff-chips code`, `GramaireNotebookIsland.tsx`), reusing
+  exactly the shape the table already gave for free. Kept, not replaced by
+  the chips: an internal debate first considered dropping the
+  Generated-tables table entirely now that the live per-rule view exists,
+  but converged on keeping both — the table is the durable, diffable
+  artifact `gramaire fmt` commits to source control; the chips are the
+  live, in-context view while editing. A collapse-by-default toggle for the
+  Generated-tables table (mirroring `diagPanelCollapsed`) was scoped out of
+  this round, tracked as a follow-up, not implemented.
+- **Literal / token / nonterminal / EOF symbol classification
+  (`SymbolKind`/`RenderedSymbol`, `LabProtocol.scala`).** A plain string
+  chip couldn't answer a real question the FIRST/FOLLOW/production views
+  raise once you actually try to read them: is `NUMBER` a token and `(` a
+  literal, or are both just "terminals"? `ProductionInfo.rhs` and
+  `RuleFirstFollow.first`/`.follow` changed from `Vector[String]` to
+  `Vector[RenderedSymbol]` (`{text, kind}`, `kind` one of `literal | token |
+  nonterminal | eof`). Classification is computed by `LabApi.scala`'s
+  `classifyTerminals` — a name-keyed `Map[String, SymbolKind]` built once
+  from the pre-`GSym` `Sym` tree (a `Sym.Lit` is `literal`, a `Sym.Ref` not
+  naming a declared rule is `token`) — deliberately kept separate from
+  `GSym` itself: `GSym.Term`'s own `equals`/`hashCode`/ordering are load-
+  bearing for `Table.scala`'s LR construction (that module's own header
+  warns it's "ported closely, not creatively"), so adding a `kind` field
+  there risked silently changing state-merging behavior in a rare symbol-
+  name-collision case. `LrActionInfo` (the Parse trace/Walk tab's step
+  stack) deliberately keeps the old string-only `renderSym` — no client
+  need for kind there yet, and every LrStepInfo consumer already treats it
+  as opaque display text. `site/src/lab/symbolDisplay.tsx` (`SymbolChip`/
+  `SymbolChips`) is the one shared rendering surface both `LabIsland.tsx`
+  (Productions/FIRST-FOLLOW tables) and the Notebook consume, coloring each
+  chip by `data-kind` — literal/token/nonterminal/EOF read as four visually
+  distinct colors (`--t-op`/`--t-term`/`--t-nonterm`/`--fg-muted`) instead
+  of one flat terminal color, matching (but not reusing — see below)
+  `Railroad.scala`'s own `DiaSym` convention.
+  `spec/lab-protocol-schema.json` gained matching `symbolKind`/
+  `renderedSymbol` `$defs`; `site/src/lab/protocol.ts` is regenerated from
+  it (`npm run gen:lab-types`), and the JVM↔JS conformance gate
+  (`check:lab-parity`) confirms both engines still produce byte-identical,
+  schema-valid responses under the new shape.
+- **One figure across Notebook, Paper, and PDF, not diagram-only.** The
+  railroad diagram and its FIRST/FOLLOW sets used to be two unrelated
+  pieces of content that happened to sit near each other, and Paper/PDF
+  showed the diagram alone — a rule's FIRST/FOLLOW was Notebook-only. Every
+  rule's figure now carries both, on every read surface: the Notebook's own
+  `.gramaire__output` div became a real `<figure>`, named by an sr-only
+  `<figcaption>` ("Railroad diagram and FIRST/FOLLOW sets for the {name}
+  rule") so assistive tech gets one accessible group instead of a labeled
+  diagram next to an unlabeled chip cluster; Paper's `PaperBlock` gained the
+  same `.gramaire__output-ff` markup inside its existing
+  `<figure>`/`<figcaption>Figure N — {name}</figcaption>`; the PDF export
+  (`paperPdf.ts`) draws FIRST/FOLLOW as kind-colored chip pills (a rounded
+  background via the existing `roundedRectPath` + plain `page.drawText`,
+  not `shapeLabel`'s HarfBuzz path — these are short plain identifiers with
+  no Fira Code ligature to worry about) below each rule's vector railroad,
+  wrapping within the content width exactly like body text already does.
+  `Railroad.scala`'s own `DiaSym` stays a two-way terminal/nonterminal
+  split, unchanged — a railroad diagram was never asked to distinguish
+  literal from token, and doing so would mean re-deriving the classifier
+  inside the diagram-construction path for no reader-facing benefit; the
+  new `ffColors`/`rrColors` in `paperPdf.ts` are intentionally two separate
+  palettes for this reason, not one merged one.
